symptom: `fmt --upgrade --header` on an mdl 0 template literal that spans lines AND has `with ({n} = …)` parameters and a backslash escape (`log info 'x\ty<LF>z {1}' with (...)`) left the escape in place, so under mdl 1 the template text held a backslash and a t instead of a tab; `'it\'s…'` even produced a script that no longer parsed.
cause: escapeFix treated every literal inside an expression whose source spans lines as stored-as-written (shouldPreserveExpressionSource -> empty fix). #746 made a multi-line template literal WITH parameters the template text under both versions, so its escapes are interpreted under mdl 0 and must be requoted.
fix: escapeFix asks templateMessageOf(top) for (template, hasParams); a template literal with parameters skips the stored-as-written shortcut and gets the requoted rewrite.
insight: When a change moves a construct from 'stored as written' to 'interpreted value' under both versions, every upgrade rewriter that branches on 'stored as written' must follow — probe the upgrade with escapes, not just line breaks.
